sourceVersionNote: Item counts and time limits verified against the official ASVAB Fact Sheet PDF retrieved from https://www.officialasvab.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ASVAB-Fact_Sheet.pdf (the October 2026 upload; identical counts also appear in the 2023-06, 2024-02 and 2025-04 editions) and officialasvab.com/applicants/cat-asvab/. CAT-ASVAB is 15/15/15/10/15/15/10/10/15/15 items = 135 items / 197 minutes; P&P-ASVAB is 25/30/35/15/25/20/25(AS)/25/25 = 225 items / 149 minutes. CAUTION: the widely circulated '16 questions, 8 minutes' figures are NOT the enlistment CAT-ASVAB; 16-item counts match the school ASVAB Career Exploration iCAT (CEP Overview, DD Form 1304-5OV, FEB 2026) and the times match no current official source. Topic lists marked in each domain note are quoted from official documents; all numeric WEIGHTS are estimates (the ASVAB program publishes no per-topic weights). Difficulty bands are official: p > .75 easy, .45 to .75 medium, < .45 hard (DMDC ASVAB Technical Bulletin No. 4, section 3.2.3). AFQT uses only AR, MK, PC and WK and is reported as a 1-99 percentile; VE = WK + PC is a derived composite, not an administered subtest. Line-score composite formulas are NOT published by the ASVAB program and must be treated as approximate.

subtests.name: General Science

domains.topic: Life science: botany, zoology, anatomy & physiology, ecology
domains.notes: Official topic list [OFFICIAL-VERIFIED]; weight estimate [ESTIMATE]. Cell/organ basics, body systems, food webs.

domains.topic: Physical science: chemistry and atomic structure
domains.notes: Elements/compounds/mixtures, states of matter, physical vs chemical change, acids-bases, catalysts.

domains.topic: Physical science: force, motion, energy, fluids
domains.notes: Density, buoyancy, energy transfer, inertia. Shallower than MC.
Planets, moon phases, eclipses, seasons (axial tilt), solar system scale.
Rock types, tectonics, weathering, fronts, water cycle, tides, atmosphere composition.

commonMistakes: Accepting a restatement as the explanation (density item answered 'it is lighter').
Confusing solar and lunar eclipse geometry.
Calling dissolving a chemical change.
Choosing the most jargon-heavy option; the pool is high-school level.
Studying advanced topics instead of the officially listed curriculum areas.
Skipping GS entirely; it feeds science/technical line scores even though it is not in the AFQT.

subtests.name: Arithmetic Reasoning

domains.topic: Multi-step whole-number word problems (rate, work, distance, unit rate)
domains.notes: Official operation list; weight [ESTIMATE]. Modal AR item, two or three operations with correct order of operations.

domains.topic: Percent, interest, discount, tax, percent change, depreciation
domains.notes: Heavily represented in official samples ($7,250 at 12% depreciation).
Part-to-part and part-to-whole ('one in every 9'), mixture and recipe scaling.

domains.topic: Rational numbers: fractions, decimals, mixed numbers
domains.notes: Fraction of a quantity in a word context; decimal equivalents.

domains.topic: Measurement, unit conversion, area/perimeter in context
domains.notes: Feet vs square feet vs square yards (official sample), gallons, time conversion.
Mean of a set, weighted average.

commonMistakes: Solving for the wrong quantity (party A instead of B; amount lost instead of value left).
Reporting the percent change instead of the resulting value.
Unit mismatch: feet vs square feet vs square yards; minutes vs hours.
Setting the proportion up upside-down.
Rounding mid-calculation and twice at the end.
Doing the arithmetic mentally instead of on the provided scratch paper, despite 3.67 minutes per item.
Leaving items blank at the time limit; the CAT penalty treats unfinished items as random guesses.

subtests.name: Word Knowledge

domains.notes: Bare stem, four one-word choices. Official format [OFFICIAL-VERIFIED]; weight [ESTIMATE].

domains.topic: Word used in a sentence, meaning resolved from context
domains.notes: Official sample: 'His record provides no reason for apprehension.'
The difficulty engine: the common meaning is the trap.

commonMistakes: Choosing a word you can define rather than the nearest synonym.
Falling for the secondary-meaning trap when the sentence pins the sense.
Letting word sound or technicality drive the choice.
Ignoring the sentence version and answering from the bare word.
Spending 90 seconds on one item in a 36-second-per-item subtest.
Studying 5,000-word lists instead of reviewing mid-frequency words with retrieval and spacing.

subtests.name: Paragraph Comprehension

domains.notes: Whole-passage synthesis; correct answer must cover the whole text. Official concept list; weight [ESTIMATE].

domains.topic: Explicit detail and reworded facts ('According to the passage')
domains.notes: Answer is verbatim or near-verbatim; tests locating, not inferring.
Answer must be forced by the text, not merely permitted.
Common word in an unusual sense inside the passage.
Usually signaled by adjectives and concessions.

domains.topic: Sequence of events / style and technique
domains.notes: Occasional 'which happened first' or 'the phrase X is used to...' item.

commonMistakes: Choosing a statement true in the world but not supported by this passage.
Answering a main-idea question with a supporting detail.
Over-inferring: accepting an inference the text permits rather than forces.
Re-reading the passage for every question instead of answering all its questions in one pass.
Ignoring absolutes ('always', 'never') that make an option indefensible.
Skipping passages on the CAT when there are only 10 items in 27 minutes.
Answering a vocabulary-in-context item from the word's most common meaning.

subtests.name: Mathematics Knowledge

domains.notes: Official bucket; weight [ESTIMATE]. Linear equations/inequalities, simplify and factor, exponent rules, identities.
Angles, triangles, Pythagorean theorem, circles, area/volume, coordinate basics.
Factors, multiples, primes, LCM/GCD, fractions/decimals, percents, roots, ratio.
Single-event probability, simple independent events.

commonMistakes: Percent direction errors (halving again instead of doubling).
Sign errors when transposing terms.
Using the diameter where the radius belongs (area is pi*r*r).
Using the favorable count instead of the total as a probability denominator.
Not recognizing factorable forms and attempting long division.
Treating MK as AR (writing equations for direct computations) or vice versa.
Unit slips in geometry: perimeter vs area vs volume, square vs cubic units.
Depending on a calculator that does not exist on the real test.

subtests.name: Electronics Information

domains.topic: Electrical quantities, symbols, units, abbreviations, meters
domains.notes: Official topic list; weight [ESTIMATE]. Volt/amp/ohm/watt, AC vs DC, schematic symbols, instrument identification.

domains.topic: DC circuits: series vs parallel, Ohm's law, resistance rules
domains.notes: The computational core: V = IR, P = VI, series/parallel behavior, one-bulb-out consequences.
Resistor, capacitor, inductor, diode, transistor, relay, transformer, fuse.
Motors, generators, alternators, batteries, ignition/charging, AC distribution.
Solder, insulation, wire gauge, conduit, fuses/breakers, grounding.

commonMistakes: Series/parallel confusion, especially the one-bulb-burns-out family.
Rearranging Ohm's law incorrectly (V = I/R) under time pressure.
Decimal-point errors with currents like 0.1 A.
Confusing resistance with conductance when the stem says 'least resistance'.
Mixing voltage (across) with current (through) when reading a schematic.
Answering from automotive intuition instead of electronics principles.
Skipping EI, which drives electronics line scores.

subtests.name: Auto & Shop Information (AI + SI)

domains.topic: Shop: hand tools, identification and correct use
domains.notes: Official area list; weight [ESTIMATE]. Rip vs crosscut vs coping vs back saws, chisels, clamps, planes, files, measuring tools.
Four-stroke cycle, piston rings, oil pump, radiator/thermostat/water pump.
Transmission/clutch concept, differential, hydraulic brakes, shock absorbers.
Drill press, circular/table saw, wood species and sheet goods, metal stock, screws/nails/bolts, adhesives.
Framing, layout, joinery, concrete/masonry basics, finishing, safety.
Battery, alternator, starter, spark plugs, ignition timing concept.
Diagnostic reasoning ('uses too much oil when which part is worn'), jack/stand safety, service tasks.

commonMistakes: Grain-direction confusion: rip vs crosscut saw (and the same error for plane blades and chisels).
Naming the part that fails because of wear rather than the part whose wear causes the symptom.
Confusing systems that share components (oil and coolant both remove heat; battery and alternator both supply electricity).
Identifying tools by silhouette instead of function (clamp, plier and wrench types).
Crossing wood and metal shop practice, or choosing the wrong fastener for the material.
Skipping the subtest on the belief that it requires prior shop class; the pool rewards general mechanical reasoning.

subtests.name: Mechanical Comprehension

domains.topic: Simple machines: levers, pulleys/block-and-tackle, inclined plane, wheel and axle, screw
domains.notes: Official topic list; weight [ESTIMATE]. MA = load/effort, effort arm/load arm, rope-segment counting.
Beam/post load sharing, center of gravity, trusses, tension vs compression.
Rotation direction, teeth-to-RPM ratio, compound trains (official: gear A 14 revs, gear B 21).
Velocity/acceleration concept, friction direction and effect, work vs power, efficiency.
Hydraulic advantage (force/area), pressure vs depth, buoyancy, valve behavior by pressure differential.
Strength/stiffness/elasticity vs plasticity, corrosion, thermal expansion, material selection.

commonMistakes: Counting rope segments wrong (count only those supporting the movable block).
Inverting the mechanical-advantage ratio (multiplying instead of dividing).
Gear-direction errors with idler gears, which reverse direction but do not change the ratio.
Assuming a longer lever is always easier regardless of fulcrum position; confusing lever classes.
Answering 'total weight' where center of gravity is the issue.
Reasoning valves by flow direction instead of pressure differential.
Treating friction as always undesirable when the item asks direction and effect.
Applying formulas where the item only asks which of four diagrams is strongest.

subtests.name: Assembling Objects

domains.topic: Fit-together (jigsaw) items: pieces rotate and translate to form one object
domains.notes: Both formats [OFFICIAL-VERIFIED]; the 60/40 split is [ESTIMATE]. Rules: rotate/translate only, never mirror, flip, stretch or rescale.

domains.topic: Connection items: match labeled attachment points on two or more pieces
domains.notes: Tests attachment-point tracking rather than silhouette matching.

commonMistakes: Selecting the answer that requires a mirrored or flipped piece.
Matching the overall silhouette while ignoring an internal notch or tab.
Assuming a piece may be scaled to fit.
Losing attachment-point correspondence in the connection format.
Mentally rotating the whole assembly when only one piece may move.
Spending too long: at 72 seconds per item, mark and move on; AO is not in the AFQT.

subtests.name: Verbal Expression (derived composite: WK + PC)

domains.topic: Word Knowledge contribution (synonyms in and out of context)
domains.notes: Derived, not administered. CAT basis 15 of 25 items; P&P basis 35 of 50 items [OFFICIAL-DERIVED].

domains.topic: Paragraph Comprehension contribution (main idea, detail, inference, tone)
domains.notes: Derived. CAT basis 10 of 25; P&P basis 15 of 50. Feeds AFQT and nearly every line score, including GT = VE + AR.

commonMistakes: Treating VE as a separate test to study, when it is only WK plus PC.
Under-investing in PC because it has only 10 CAT items while it contributes 40% of VE.
Ignoring VE when selecting an enlistment goal, since GT = VE + AR gates a large share of technical jobs.

studyTechniques.name: Retrieval practice (practice testing)
studyTechniques.what: Make every review interaction a question the learner must answer before seeing the explanation; never present a summary screen as the primary review loop.
studyTechniques.evidence: Dunlosky, Rawson, Marsh, Nathan and Willingham (2013), Psychological Science in the Public Interest 14(1), 4-58 - rated high utility. Meta-analytic g about 0.50 (Rowland, 2014, Psychological Bulletin 140(6), 1432-1463); g about 0.61 for practice testing versus restudy (Adesope, Trevisan and Sundararajan, 2017, Review of Educational Research 87(3), 659-701).

studyTechniques.name: Spaced repetition (distributed practice)
studyTechniques.what: Schedule expanding review intervals tied to mastery, with the final review just before the test date; scale the lag to the retention interval.
studyTechniques.evidence: Cepeda, Pashler, Vul, Wixted and Rohrer (2006), Psychological Bulletin 132(3), 354-380; Cepeda et al. (2008), Psychological Science 19(11), 1095-1102 - optimal gap about 10-20% of retention interval; Dunlosky et al. (2013) - high utility.

studyTechniques.name: Interleaving
studyTechniques.what: Mix item types within a session (AR: ratio, percent, rate; MK: algebra, geometry, number theory) instead of blocking one type.
studyTechniques.evidence: Rohrer and Taylor (2007), Instructional Science 35, 481-498; Taylor and Rohrer (2010), JARMAC; Brunmair and Richter (2019), Psychological Bulletin 145(11), 1029-1052 - overall g about 0.42, largest for inductive category learning.

studyTechniques.name: Worked-example fading
studyTechniques.what: For AR, MK, EI and MC, introduce each new item type with a full worked example, then a completion problem with the last step blank, then a standard item; fade the scaffolds as accuracy rises.
studyTechniques.evidence: Sweller and Cooper (1985), Cognition and Instruction 2(1), 59-89; Renkl and Atkinson (2003) on fading; Kalyuga, Ayres, Chandler and Sweller (2003) - expertise reversal effect, so stop scaffolding once competent.

studyTechniques.name: Elaborative interrogation and self-explanation
studyTechniques.what: After each answer, require an explanation of why the key is right and why the most attractive distractor is wrong; store one reinforcement lesson per misconception.
studyTechniques.evidence: Dunlosky et al. (2013) - moderate utility; Bisra, Liu, Nesbit, Salimi and Winne (2018), Educational Psychology Review 30, 703-725 - self-explanation prompting g about 0.55.

studyTechniques.name: Error-focused corrective feedback
studyTechniques.what: Immediate, specific feedback that names the error class (wrong quantity, semantic neighbor, inverted ratio), then requeue that item type after a delay.
studyTechniques.evidence: Butler and Roediger (2008), European Journal of Cognitive Psychology - the testing effect is larger with feedback; Hattie and Timperley (2007), Review of Educational Research 77(1), 81-112.

studyTechniques.name: Metacognitive calibration
studyTechniques.what: Collect a confidence rating before revealing correctness and teach the gap between recognition and production.
studyTechniques.evidence: Koriat and Bjork (2005), Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition 31(2), 187-194; Dunlosky et al. (2013) on judgment-of-learning overconfidence.

studyTechniques.name: Format-specific guessing strategy
studyTechniques.what: P&P: never leave a bubble empty, there is no guessing penalty. CAT/PiCAT/APT: do not blind-guess; unfinished items are scored as random responses and answers cannot be reviewed.
studyTechniques.evidence: OFFICIAL: ASVAB Fact Sheet (2026 edition), pages 1 and 4; officialasvab.com/researchers/scores/ - CAT penalty function is equivalent to random guessing on unfinished items.
